nodes.question: Compare the source and edited images: identify the original blue mug by its appearance and track that same object in the edited image, distinguishing it from any other mugs. Where is that same mug relative to the headphones, and has it moved rightward from its source position?
nodes.criteria: complete only if the same mug visible in the source is identifiable in the edited image and is now to the right of the headphones. partial if that same mug has moved rightward toward the right-of-headphones target but is not yet to their right. absent if the same mug shows no progress toward the target. unknown if its identity, position, or movement cannot be established from the images. Do not count another mug appearing to the right, or disappearance of the original mug, as completion or progress.
nodes.binding: Source object: the blue mug with a handle, left of the black headphones. Reference object: the black over-ear headphones. Track the source mug across the edited image; do not substitute other mugs.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
